newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: Lurgi signs Saudi chemical plant deal.
newsitem.headline: Lurgi signs Saudi chemical plant deal.

text.p: A Saudi-Taiwanese joint venture said on Monday it had signed a letter of intent with German engineering group Lurgi to undertake basic engineering design for a new chemical plant.
Al-Jubail Fertiliser Company (SAMAD) said the new plant would be built in the eastern industrial city of al-Jubail to produce 50,000 tonnes a year of phthalic anhydride.
It said the plant, scheduled to come on stream in the fourth quarter of 1999, would use the "Wacker process" to produce phthalic anhydride. It did not elaborate or give a cost of the project.
SAMAD is a 50-50 owned by Saudi Arabia's industrial giant Saudi Basic Industries Corp (SABIC) and state-owned Taiwan Fertiliser Co.
SABIC's vice-chairman and managing director, Ibrahim Bin Salameh, said the project, the first in the Middle East, was the final phase of SAMAD's current expansion programme.
He said 60 percent of the project's output would be exported.
The plant's products are mainly used in the production of alkyd resins, unsaturated polyester resins, dyes, perfumes, insecticides, pharmaceuticals and resin hardeners.

SABIC, 70 percent owned by the Saudi government, accounts for five percent of total world production of petrochemicals. It operates and controls 16 complexes with Japanese and Western firms producing around 23 million tonnes annually.
